    Recently, I was offered a last minute spot to fundraise and run the 2026 NYC Marathon on November 1 with Every Mother Counts — to which I gladly accepted.

    My mom, Maureen, has always been my biggest supporter. She has believed in me, encouraged me, and cheered me on through every stage of my life. I’m running this marathon for her, and for the belief that everyone deserves the chance to know and grow up with their mom.

    is a nonprofit working to make pregnancy and childbirth safer for mothers globally. EMC supports programs and advocates for systems that help ensure mothers can receive respectful, quality maternity care, wherever they live.

    Left with roughly 40 days to train and raise $4,000, I’m grateful to have the chance to run for this mission. Support, at any level, means a lot.

    Thank you,Brayden

      Where the money actually goes

      They have been at this for fifteen years.

      2010Founded by Christy Turlington Burns, after she nearly died giving birth
      $48M+Invested in community-led programs, advocacy and awareness
      ~2MWomen, families and health workers supported so far
      2 minHow often a woman dies somewhere in the world from pregnancy or childbirth

      Every Mother Counts funds and partners with community-led maternal health programs. In practice that means training midwives and community health workers, covering the cost of getting a woman to a clinic, and equipping the facilities she arrives at. The organization also campaigns for policy change and works to put the issue in front of people who would otherwise never hear about it.

      The problem is larger than most people assume. Somewhere in the world a woman dies roughly every two minutes from causes tied to pregnancy or childbirth, and most of those deaths are preventable. The United States has the highest maternal mortality rate of any wealthy country, and the burden falls hardest on Black and Indigenous women. This is not only a problem somewhere else.

      Since launching in 2010, Every Mother Counts has invested more than $48 million and reached close to two million women, families and health workers, working in the United States alongside Haiti, Uganda, Bangladesh, India, Tanzania and Guatemala. It was founded by Christy Turlington Burns, who hemorrhaged after her own daughter was born in 2003 and survived because she happened to be somewhere with people who knew what to do. She made a documentary about it, No Woman, No Cry, and then built the organization.

      There is a reason this charity is so tied up with running. Turlington Burns first thought of distance running as a way to talk about pregnancy and birth while she was training for the New York City Marathon. Her team made a film, Every Mile, Every Mother, about exactly that: how far a woman may have to travel before she reaches anyone qualified to help her deliver.
